issue.title: Stabilize TaskMirror detached-count test under suite load
issue.description: In the 13-worker just test run on 2026-08-02, tests/ace/tui/test_task_mirror.py::test_mirror_counts_global_detached_and_this_sessions_command_tasks failed after 17.69s because TaskMirror._refresh_detached_count() had not invoked on_detached_count (counts was [] instead of [2]). The test passed alone immediately afterward in 0.05s. Diagnose and remove the suite-load timing dependency so the callback assertion is deterministic under xdist.

evidence.note: Independent recurrence during unrelated epic-launch sync-lock implementation on 2026-08-03: full just check failed tests/ace/tui/test_task_mirror.py::test_mirror_counts_global_detached_and_this_sessions_command_tasks after 25,825 passes / 7 skips, while the exact node passed immediately afterward in isolation with .venv/bin/pytest -vv (1 passed in 0.76s). This matches the existing suite-load timing signature.

payload.close_reason: Backlog triage 2026-08-05: consolidating the full-parallel-suite / xdist flake class onto umbrella task sase-ct ('Flaky ACE TUI tests under full parallel just test run'). Every one of these reports the same shape — a single node fails under the full four-to-27-worker 'just test' or 'just check' run and passes immediately in isolation — so they share a root-cause class (xdist load sensitivity and shared-state leakage across workers) rather than per-test logic bugs. Per-test detail, including sase-cu's pump-free clipboard-task diagnosis, stays readable on each bead, and a +1 with fresh evidence reopens any of them if a specific node turns into a deterministic failure.
